sources.title: Basic Audio Oscix 2020 - Blue - Reverb
sources.excerpt:
- **Archive parent:** Oscix
- **Builder:** Basic Audio
- **Catalog type:** Fuzz
- **Identity:** Germanium oscillating fuzz derived from Fuzz Face/Fuzz Factory concepts, with extensive external control over bias, supply starvation, gating and oscillation. [1][2]

- **LEVEL**
- **STARVE**
- **FUZZ**
- **GATE**
- **PINCH**
- **OSC**
- **VINTAGE** toggle
- **FAT** toggle [1][2]

The controls interact strongly, allowing both conventional fuzz and deliberately unstable self-oscillating behavior.

- **Fuzz Face / Fuzz Factory-style germanium architecture.**
- The archive records this as a lineage relationship rather than claiming exact schematic identity with either historical pedal. [1][2]

- **Technology:** Germanium.
- Exact production transistor part number is not publicly documented.

- Exact clipping-device type and part number are not publicly documented.

- **9V center-negative** operation with battery support is documented by the Basic Audio product system.

- No numbered electronic revision established.
- Multiple photographs on the product page represent production examples/angles rather than separate revisions.

Oscix is designed to cross the line between fuzz and electronic instrument: Bias/Starve/Gate/Pinch can choke or distort the signal while OSC can push it into controlled squeal and self-oscillation. The Vintage and Fat functions add further tonal shifts around the core response. [1][2]

- **Identity:** High
- **Germanium technology:** High
- **Oscillation controls:** High
- **Fuzz Face/Fuzz Factory lineage:** High as builder description
- **Exact transistor:** Unknown
- **Exact diode:** Unknown

Basic Audio's Oscix page was cross-checked with Guitar Pedal X's dedicated oscillating-fuzz overview. The evidence supports the control set, Germanium implementation and intentional self-oscillation architecture. Exact semiconductor part numbers remain unpublished. [1][2]

1. Basic Audio — Oscix: https://www.basicaudio.net/store-1/5einpey75gjgckjedkvplbsbfsb3vnya-y3hb9-97e3s-cnzrr-gbrkf-l5lts-pjhh6
2. Guitar Pedal X — 15 Notable Trem-Fuzzes and Oscillating-Fuzzes: https://www.guitarpedalx.com/news/15-notable-trem-fuzzes-and-oscillating-fuzzes

- **Exact pedal photograph:** Basic Audio official product photograph.
- **Direct image:** https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5da9e97016ddf940acffa2d/1650847714009-V81QID62II24NWUIZTQ6/DSCF6453_1.jpg
- **Source page:** Basic Audio Oscix product page.

This pass adds only claims supported by the newly admitted exact-model evidence. Earlier archive research is retained unchanged.

Oscix — Basic Audio Contact Store About Menu Basic Audio Contact Store About Pedal colors are subject to change.

- The evidence references: MKI, MKIII, revision, v1.

- Germanium Fuzz.

Dual 3-way Vintage and Fat switches to control low end saturation pre and post circuit fuzz.

May 23, 2022 08:00 by  Stefan Karlsson Basic Audio Big Muff Style Fuzz Fuzz Fuzz Face Style Fuzz Fuzz-Drive and Fuzzstortion Gated and Velcro Fuzz Germanium Fuzz Maestro Style Fuzz Modulated Fuzz Octave Fuzz Oddball Fuzz OpAmp Fuzz Oscillating Fuzz Rat Style Fuzz Silicon Fuzz Super-Fuzz Style Tone Bender Style Fuzz + - Full Article Read Summary Key Points We own 19 Basic Audio fuzzes and note John Lyons’ range: about 40 active pedals and roughly 100 different varieties made over the years. Favorites include Scarab Deluxe, Alter‑Destiny, Spooky Tooth, Wildcat and Zippy. There are ~33 other Basic Audio circuits available; a broad target list shows many with prices (examples: Beeb‑Ah Fuzz $200, Buzztone Fuzzy‑Drive $200, Bye‑Bias Germanium Dual Bias $220, OSCIX Germanium Fuzz Factory $220, Super Fuzz $210). Ten front‑runners are highlighted for possible purchase. Common suppliers: The Sound Parcel, CoastSonic, Electric Mojo, Rogue Guitar Shop, SoCal Amplification; 26 Basic Audio pedals currently listed on Reverb. John can custom‑make some semi‑retired fuzzes when parts permit. Readers should know by now that I’m a huge fan of ’King of Fuzz’ John Lyons and his Basic Audio Imprint. I don’t believe anyone is more prolific than John - who has turned his hand to pretty much every fuzz variety there has been over the years. With a superb quality approach which marries practicality with aesthetics, extended features and superior sounds! His current active pedal range consists of around 40 key fuzz varieties, while over the years he must have made around 100 different varieties and variations of pedals - a pretty incredible achievement all told. I’ve been collecting Basic Audio Fuzzes for a number of years now - acquiring them from a variety of sources - mostly in the USA, but pretty much the four corners of the globe too - throughout Europe and as far afield as Japan and Singapore! To-date I have 19 of John’s fuzzes in the collection - exactly the varieties pictured above - in those enclosures / colours : Alter-Destiny Fuzz (All-Rounder Modern + Articulate Big Muff) Foxey Lady Fuzz (Guild Foxey Lady Muff) Foxton Octave Fuzz (Foxx Tone Machine) Futureman (Colorsound Power Boost / Overdriver) Fuzzmondo (Fuzzrite-ish Silicon Fuzz) Fuzz Mutant (Os Mutantes Regulus VIII) Gnarly Fuzz (Maestro/Tone Bender) Gypsy Fuzz (KR Musical Products The Gypsy Fuzz) Marq Won Germanium Fuzz (Tone Bender MKI) Nonts (Silicon Baldwin-Burns Buzzaround) Orpheum II Germanium Fuzz (Germanium Fuzz Face) Scarab Deluxe Fuzz (All-Rounder Silicon Tone Bender) Shore Bird Fuzz/Dist
